decisions.label: Overlap I/O
decisions.brief: Off: the experts are computed on the device, beside its cache.
decisions.reason: overlap hides the CPU's expert compute behind the streamer's reads, and with the device expert cache armed the experts are computed on CUDA1, so there is nothing on the CPU for it to hide

decisions.label: Device expert cache
decisions.brief: A 13.1 GiB cache of the most used experts on CUDA1, in place of whole layers' experts.
decisions.reason: the experts used most live on the processor that computes them fastest, as the RAM cache holds what flash would read: CUDA1 computes this model's experts at 544 GiB/s against the host's 254, both measured on this model's own expert block; a cache of 13419 MiB (13174 the capacity fitter gave 10 of 89 layers' experts, 245 it left free under one more whole layer) serves 11% of a token's routed bytes (the fraction of the expert set it holds); a miss is uploaded from the host

decisions.label: Batch width
decisions.brief: A prompt runs in one pass: that takes only 1.8 GiB.
decisions.reason: a graph as wide as the context reserves 1792 MiB of compute buffers, inside 10% of the 247009 MiB this process may hold: a prompt is computed in one pass

decisions.label: Layer placement
decisions.brief: 93 layers on a device; 89 of 89 layers keep their experts on the CPU.
decisions.reason: the capacity fitter found a placement that is projected to fit; 89 of 89 MoE layers keep their experts on the host, host-resident 1826 MiB, on devices 32197 MiB, context 16384 (fitter's host breakdown: model 102584, context 34, compute 1792 MiB; file 127032, experts 117253)

decisions.label: Context
decisions.brief: 16384 tokens of context, as given: not weighed against the cache.
decisions.reason: the value this run was given, not a choice: the capacity fitter only picks a context when it is handed a zero and this planner always pins it, so nothing has weighed this number against what the memory it reserves would buy as expert cache

decisions.label: Streaming mode
decisions.brief: The whole model (116.3 GiB) fits in the 193.0 GiB usable.
decisions.reason: on the host 119137 MiB (dense 1884) against 197607 MiB usable, which is the 247009 MiB this process may hold (as reported available, unmeasured) less a 49401 MiB margin (the process is killed)

decisions.label: Experts in a device's host memory
decisions.brief: The device cache uploads from the file's mapping.
decisions.reason: a miss reaches CUDA1 at 11.3 GiB/s from the file's mapping and at 20.8 from the backend's own host memory, but the copy's 117253 MiB beside the 119137 MiB the host already holds is past the 197607 MiB it may

decisions.label: Expert streaming
decisions.brief: Not streamed: the whole model fits in memory.
decisions.reason: the host residual fits: llama.cpp's placement is the whole plan

decisions.label: Compute threads
decisions.brief: 47 threads: the fastest count measured on this model's format.
decisions.reason: swept over the thread counts this machine has, on a matmul in this model's own quantized format, which is the material that matters: a sweep in F32 can pick a count the quantized kernels are much slower at

decisions.label: Thread counts to measure
decisions.brief: The first answer measures 23 threads against 47.
decisions.reason: the thread count changes no output and which one decodes fastest is this machine's answer, not a rule's: once the cache has settled the first real request alternates decode windows between 47 and 23 (where a slower class of core starts, every core, or half of them where all are alike), and switches only to a count 10% faster in the median of its rounds; the next load starts from the verdict
